question: How many cumulative locally acquired 2026 dengue cases will Hillsborough County, Florida show in the Florida Arbovirus Surveillance report published on or around September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class is Florida county-level locally acquired dengue clusters two weekly-report steps past the ~50-60 mark, anchored on this outbreak's own report series (W32 15 -> W33 30 -> W34 59). A ~2.0x two-step multiplier gives a base rate near 118. Adjustments: (a) the Sep 18 report most likely covers onsets through Sep 12 (W36), since W35 was still a 404 today and the observed cadence is Thursday publication ~5 days after week end - but ~15-20% of the time only W35 (through Sep 5) is available, which shifts the low tail down; (b) the observed increments (+15, +29) partly reflect an ascertainment ramp after the Jul 31 alert plus onset-week backfill, and both saturate, so a third and fourth doubling is unlikely though not negligible; (c) aerial adulticiding only started Sep 5-6 and dengue's ~2.5-week human-mosquito-human generation time means the weeks being counted were largely seeded before control took hold, so I do not expect a sharp break inside the window; (d) counts by onset date essentially never revise downward, so 59 is a hard floor and the lower bound is unreachable. Two continued doublings (-> ~230) is the concrete upper-escape mechanism, priced at 7%. Evidence is one-sided in the sense that no source yet reports a plateau - I found no post-Sep-5 case data at all - which is a real gap and keeps me near the base-rate multiplier rather than extrapolating the doubling. No prediction market prices this question.

calls.reconciliation: Two factual disputes were settled from the dossiers. (a) Publication cadence: Run 2 claimed Friday posting inferred from news timing; Runs 1 and 3 said Thursday, and Run 3's read of the PDFs' own printed dates (w31 Fri Aug 14, w32 Thu Aug 20, w33 Thu Aug 27, w34 Thu Sep 3) is direct primary evidence that beats an inference from when WUSF wrote its story. Settled: Thursday, ~5 days after the Saturday week-end, so w36 posts ~Sep 17 and the w35-only branch drops from Run 2's 18% to ~12%. (b) The w31 value: Run 1 could not find it, Run 3 read 5 from the PDF; adopted, completing the increment series +3/+10/+15/+29. (c) The Background text's 'Week 37 (Sep 6-12)' is an off-by-one on the week number only; all runs agree the resolving onset range is Sep 6-12. Unsettleable: whether the +29 was genuine acceleration or partly a lab catch-up batch — FDOH publishes onset-MONTH granularity only, so no weekly curve exists to decide it, and that uncertainty is carried in the width rather than resolved by fiat. On the pure-judgment dispute over reference class, I take the outbreak's own series as the anchor (full-season county totals average over clusters that never got this large) while letting the historical maximum of ~161 pull the median down from naive extrapolation. I did not average the runs: I re-derived the number bottom-up by calibrating a reporting-completeness curve on the July-onset revisions and applying it to the August and early-September onset cohorts, which independently produced 105-135 central with a 104-152 parameter sweep. The resulting median of 117 sits inside the runs' 115-122 spread because that is where my own reconstruction lands, and my narrower width reflects the cadence dispute being settled rather than any hedging. All three runs and the harness search agree no market prices this; no crowd blend applied.
